## Proposal (operator-adjudicated — filed from measurement 50e3-6d2a, not implemented)

The measurement on 50e3-6d2a-0e7f-4e92 found the 88 recorded caused_by edges cannot be
partitioned into blame-derived guesses vs explicitly supplied attributions: `_apply_caused_by`
(src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py) writes both through `_write_link_event` with no
provenance field. Consequences measured there:

- The population study could only BOUND the derived share (38 consistent-with-blame / 6
  divergent / 44 not reproducible today).
- On the only 8 edges with independently proven origins, the deriver scored 0 correct,
  1 confidently wrong (named the innocent producer), 7 abstained — yet on read a guessed edge
  is indistinguishable from those proven ones, so escape-rate lenses and the epic-close
  caused_by floor weight them identically.

## Proposed change (small, schema-level)

Add a `derived: blame | explicit` (or equivalent) field to the caused_by LINK event at the two
write sites in transition_close.py, defaulting old events to unknown on read. Consumers
(`rebar metrics` escape-rate lenses) may then report supplied vs derived rates separately or
discount derived edges. NO change to the deriver's fail-closed behaviour is proposed — the
measurement found the strict-majority abstention is working as designed.

## Why filed, not done

Schema/gate-adjacent changes are operator-adjudicated per project policy. This ticket is the
proposal; the evidence base is the findings comment on 50e3-6d2a-0e7f-4e92.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Operator decision recorded on this ticket (accept/reject/amend the marker design).
- [ ] If accepted: link event schema carries the marker, both write sites populate it, old
      events read as unknown, and docs/event-schema.md documents it.
- [ ] If accepted: rebar metrics distinguishes supplied vs derived caused_by edges in at least
      the escape-rate lens.
compiled_state.title: Proposal: provenance marker (derived vs explicit) on caused_by link events
